science.title: Cells pulse together as they grow-and malignant cells pulse the longest
science.description: Epithelial cells are the tiny shields that line and protect our bodies. In a developing embryo, epithelial cells grow, divide and move into positions to form the outer layers of our skin and the surfaces of our organs and blood vessels. When we scrape our skin, suffer an internal tear or undergo surgery, epithelial cells migrate to the site of injury to heal a wound. And when epithelial cells go haywire, they can turn malignant and spread through the body as cancer.

science.title: CAM-RTDETR: an aerospace engine surface defect detection method based on improved transformer architecture
science.description: To address challenges in the surface defect detection of core Aerospace Engine components, specifically targeting texture aliasing under strong metallic backgrounds and the difficulty in identifying cross-scale minute defects such as tiny dots, this paper proposes CAM-RTDETR, a detection model based on an improved RT-DETR-r18. First, to accommodate the irregular geometry of blades, a C2f-DBlock backbone based on Multi-Branch Dilated Convolutions is designed to effectively decouple defect features from the rigid background grid. Second, a Texture-Sensitive Self-Attention (AIFI-TSSA) module is introduced into the Encoder, incorporating learnable texture biases to suppress the interference of high-frequency metallic grain noise. Finally, a Mixed Aggregation Network (MANet) is adopted to replace the standard fusion module, utilizing a multi-branch structure to preserve the faint signals of minute defects during feature fusion. Experimental results on a self-constructed Aerospace Engine defect dataset indicate that, while maintaining real-time performance, the proposed method reduces parameter count by 21.5% and computational cost (GFLOPs) by 16.1% compared to the baseline RT-DETR-r18. Furthermore, it achieves a 1.7% increase in mAP@0.5–0.95 and a 4.0% increase in Precision. Compared with mainstream YOLO series models, the method demonstrates significant performance advantages in detecting minute defects and low-contrast scratches.

science.title: Dual-channel 1D-CNN-BiLSTM transfer learning for diagnosing tooth breakage across circular saw blade wear stages
science.description: As the core cutting tool for dismantling stainless steel cladding of spent fuel assemblies, the circular saw blade is prone to tooth breakage failure, which can directly lead to reduced machining accuracy, decreased production efficiency, and even equipment safety accidents. Furthermore, dynamic changes in the wear stage of the circular saw blade cause shifts in the distribution characteristics of cutting signals, posing a challenge for domain adaptation in cross-wear stage tooth breakage diagnosis. To address the issues of scarce fault annotation data for each wear stage in actual production and the insufficient generalization ability of traditional models, this paper proposes a transfer learning fault diagnosis method based on a dual-channel 1D-CNN-BiLSTM network. First, the method effectively preprocesses dual-channel vibration signals during circular saw blade cutting, including effective signal extraction and sliding window framing, to construct a source-domain fault dataset for new saw blade tooth breakage and target-domain datasets for each wear stage. Subsequently, a hybrid 1D-CNN-BiLSTM network is designed, where 1D-CNN extracts multi-scale local spatial features of the saw blade cutting signals, and BiLSTM captures bidirectional temporal dependency features. This network is pre-trained in the source domain as a general fault feature extraction model. Finally, a fine-tuning strategy combining layer replacement and adaptive learning rate factors is adopted, freezing the bottom feature extraction layers and retraining the top classification layer, thereby achieving efficient transfer of fault knowledge from the source domain (new saw blade tooth breakage) to the target domain (various wear stages). Using three types of circular saw blade tooth breakage as the research object and comparing with methods such as SVM, 1D-CNN, LSTM, ResNet and DANN, experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 97.9% in cross-wear stage tooth breakage fault diagnosis, significantly outperforming other methods. It effectively solves the transfer diagnosis problem of tooth breakage faults across wear stages and improves the cutting efficiency of stainless steel cladding of spent fuel assemblies.
